narrative: A year of module-by-module outages (exports, alerts, report builder, dashboards) escalated in May 2025 into an explicit demand to escalate beyond first-line support ("I need this escalated beyond first-line support... nobody has given us a straight answer"), but from June onward every ticket is calm-to-positive, including thanks for a quick dashboard-speed fix and two new seats added in September. The shift from crisis language to routine how-to questions and seat growth is a genuine recovery, not just a lull.

Five tickets over seven months, all low-key: a formatting question resolved and explicitly confirmed working ("working well now, thanks"), a drill-down feature request followed up politely, and a new seat added for a hire. No faults, no frustration - a quiet, healthy account.

High-frequency technical churn - a multi-system outage in August 2024 (connector, exports, admin, API all down within days) and another cluster in February 2025 - but every incident is resolved in 1-2 days and the customer keeps coming back with new requests rather than pulling away. The one real red flag is the February ticket noting the connector fault is happening "again - the ERP connector from back in August has stopped syncing, same symptoms," meaning that specific fault line recurred, but the fast-resolution pattern otherwise reads as an engaged, if operationally noisy, relationship.
Two routine tickets, a formatting question and a dashboard refresh question, both resolved within days with no complaint. Nothing here suggests any account health concern.

An alert rule that misfired twice in February 2025 ("might be worth checking the underlying logic rather than just the config") is the only real friction, and it isn't mentioned again after being marked resolved. The rest of the ticket history - chart types, seat renewal timing, a new connector - is calm, routine, and spread out.

Four purely informational tickets over two months - export limits, report builder access for a new team, API documentation gaps. No faults reported, no frustration, and the account is actively provisioning for growth (new regional team).

A slow-burning API/export problem from autumn 2024 went unresolved for months and resurfaced as dashboard outages into 2025, culminating in an explicit escalation demand in June 2025 ("I'd like to get on a call with someone senior... email back-and-forth isn't cutting it anymore"). Critically, the call happened, and every ticket after August 2025 is calm or positive ("thanks for the call", "noticeably faster", "now that things are stable") including two expansion requests (real-time refresh, a new connector) - a genuine recovery, not a lull, with one trivial cosmetic issue still open.

A brutal run of chronic outages across nearly every module from late 2024 through May 2025 pushed the customer to explicitly question whether "we're starting to question whether this platform can support daily operations reliably" and to escalate twice ("I want to speak to someone above first-line support"). The August 2025 admin-lockout ticket is the turning point: the customer calls the explanation "actually useful - first time in a while I've felt like someone properly looked under the hood," and every ticket since is positive, including an explicit before/after distinction ("a real change, not just a lull before the next outage") and active growth (new seats, usage checks ahead of scaling).

competitor_mentions.quote: One of our other business units evaluated Dashlume recently and their dashboard export includes a one-click PowerPoint format - is that something Kataja has, or is planning?

narrative: Three tickets across three months, all administrative or informational. One casual comparison to Dashlume's PowerPoint export is a feature curiosity, not a procurement signal. Healthy, low-touch account.

Timo's account is the quiet-danger pattern the brief warns about: sparse tickets (six over 13 months), each more measured than the last, tracking real unresolved problems - a January question about declining dashboard usage that never got a useful answer, a February alert-silent-failure ticket that says so directly ("I submitted a ticket in January... and haven't had a useful response"), and export failures recurring three times by May ("I raised this in January, I raised it in February, and here we are in May"). The July ticket is a one-line, resigned "I've written it three times already... Please fix it" - asks are shrinking exactly as volume drops, with no anger, just accumulating distrust.

Four low-friction tickets over eight months - connector setup, a sync feature request, an alert question, a new seat request still pending. No complaints, no repeated faults; a normal light-touch account.

Three widely-spaced tickets over 13 months, all calm information requests (a new banking connector, a board-template export idea, alert setup help). Sparse but neutral in tone throughout - the healthy kind of quiet.

Pekka's account shows the exact dangerous pattern the brief warns about: a dashboard/export reconciliation mismatch in June 2025 where "two of my colleagues have gone back to reconciling manually in Excel before each board pack, just so we're not presenting numbers we can't trust," followed a month later by a report-builder template reverting for the third time since spring, where the team has "started keeping a saved copy on our side" and explicitly says "no need to treat this as urgent." Both tickets are marked resolved, but the customer has quietly built workarounds around problems that keep recurring and is asking for less each time, not more.

A relentless two-year run of outages across every module (API, exports, connectors, dashboards, admin), but the defining feature is that the customer keeps trusting the team to fix things fast and says so repeatedly ("you've always turned these around fast", "you always fix these fast - please make this one just as quick"). The complaint that surfaces late (June 2025) is about frequency, not competence, and there is no escalation demand or drop-off - a loud but engaged account.
Five tickets over nine months, entirely feature questions and setup help (templates, Google Sheets, dashboard comments, connector alerts). Calm, curious, and healthy throughout.
A single routine seat-transfer request, resolved in five days. No signal of any concern.

Emma's account deteriorates clearly: a calculated-fields bug from April 2024 is marked unresolved and referenced as still broken in two later tickets, a dashboard-staleness fault is called "a meaningful reliability problem," and by June she is asking whether the platform is "fit for purpose." The July 2024 ticket ties a recurring connector fault ("fixed" in March, same symptoms four months later) to an explicit statement that she is "documenting all of this because our contract is up for renewal and I will need to make a case either way" - the clearest renewal-risk language in this batch - and the account goes silent afterward.
Seven tickets over 13 months, all how-to and feature questions (themes, viewer seats, scheduled reports, a UI-move flagged as "not a complaint"). Consistently calm and low-stakes.

Extremely high incident volume across almost every module, but the customer stays actively engaged rather than going quiet or resigned, and most fixes land within a day or two. The clearest recurring thread is the October 2025 connector fault, down twice in three days ("would help to know if this is a recurring root cause rather than a one-off each time"), and an April frustration note about frequency rather than competence - chronic but not clearly heading for the door.

competitor_mentions.quote: as part of next year's tooling review we've been asked to take a look at Dashlume alongside our renewal, so if there's anything worth knowing about the roadmap for connector reliability, I'd welcome the context.

narrative: A professional, low-drama account until May 2025, when a connector-mapping ticket casually notes that "as part of next year's tooling review we've been asked to take a look at Dashlume alongside our renewal" - a serious, renewal-tied competitor mention. The July ticket about slow dashboard loads compounds the signal: the team has quietly moved to a scheduled-export workaround and explicitly flags "no particular urgency... wanted it on record" - the same low-urgency, workaround-accepting tone the guidance flags as the real danger sign, not the louder complaints elsewhere in the batch.
